tldr: MedReason introduces a large-scale medical reasoning dataset generated by converting clinical QA pairs into knowledge-graph-grounded chain-of-thought explanations, enabling faithful and explainable medical problem-solving in LLMs.
contributions: MedReason dataset of 32,682 high-quality question-answer pairs with step-by-step CoT explanations grounded in the PrimeKG medical knowledge graph
A novel data generation pipeline that retrieves reasoning paths from a KG and uses them as scaffolds for medically grounded CoT generation
Empirical demonstration that fine-tuning with MedReason consistently improves medical reasoning across diverse 7-8B parameter models, achieving state-of-the-art performance on clinical benchmarks
methods: The pipeline extracts medical entities from QA pairs and maps them to nodes in the PrimeKG knowledge graph using a three-stage matching process (exact match, similarity match with threshold 0.85, and LLM-based selection). Shortest paths between question and answer entities are retrieved, then pruned by an LLM to retain the 3 most relevant paths. These paths serve as structural scaffolds for an LLM to generate CoT explanations. Finally, quality filtering is applied by having an LLM answer the question using only the generated CoT; only samples producing the correct answer are retained (32,682 out of 45,000 generated samples).
results: Fine-tuning LLaMA 3.1-Instruct-8B with MedReason improved average accuracy from 45.8% to 51.2% (+5.4%). Mistral-Instruct-7B improved from 36.1% to 44.7% (+8.6%). DeepSeek-Distill-8B gained up to 7.7% on challenging clinical datasets. MedReason-8B (fine-tuned from Huatuo-o1-RL-8B) achieved the highest average score of 57.3% across five benchmarks, outperforming Huatuo-o1-8B by up to 4.2% on MedBullets. Expert physicians from seven clinical specialties validated the dataset quality.
limitations: The pipeline excludes QA pairs where entities cannot be extracted (e.g., numerical answers), reducing the initial 55K QA pairs to 45K for generation. The approach depends on the coverage of the PrimeKG knowledge graph for entity mapping and path retrieval. Quality filtering retained only 32,682 of 45,000 generated samples (~73%), discarding low-quality reasoning traces.
